dossier.architecture: Compact turret with omnidirectional note feed and lightweight auxiliary endgame.

subsystems.drivetrain: Narrow SDS modules create room for the note path; module standoffs help define the feeder cage.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper intake feeds four vertical rollers.
subsystems.transfer: Rotating rollers draw the note around the cage into the turret at different headings.
subsystems.scoring: Continuously aiming turret; lightweight amp bar guides an upward shot.
subsystems.endgame: Late-added light climber uses a worm drive to resist backdrive.
subsystems.controls: Turret-mounted Limelight requires moving-camera pose transforms; superstructure states coordinate mechanisms.

versions: Conceptual feed prototype validated before detailed design. Climber added after prioritizing the main scoring architecture.
dossier.analysis: A turret is useful only if its feed remains viable across turret headings. Narrow modules and a shared cage are enabling packaging choices, not incidental component preferences.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.title: 2024-2910 · Any-heading note loading is the prerequisite for a useful turret
context_documents.body:
# 2024-2910: Any-heading note loading is the prerequisite for a useful turret

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Under-bumper acquisition feeds four vertical rollers that move the note around the turret’s receiving cage. A light amp guide directs an upward release. The source describes a late, simple worm-drive climb and software superstates that coordinate turret, feeder and launcher rather than binding unrelated commands independently.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly emphasizes feeding at different turret headings. Climb packaging was constrained by its late addition, motivating simplicity and low mass.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A turret adds little directional independence if it must return to one heading to acquire every note. The receiving cage and its contact sequence are therefore as important as aiming range. A superstate helps express the common readiness condition, but needs fault handling when only some mechanisms reach their setpoints. A worm transmission should not be assumed to hold every load without checking its actual efficiency and disabled behavior.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure transfer success versus heading, note wear and acceleration. Test partial readiness, cable limits and power-off climb retention. The viewer-disabled binder remains unreviewed; do not substitute a guessed download.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/AefyOa_38F8](https://youtu.be/AefyOa_38F8)

source_reviews.title: Jack in the Bot Typhoon release
source_reviews.locator: Posts 1, 2 and reply on any-angle feed
facts: Two entry points serve the intake-facing half of the feed. Team reports reliable feed at any turret angle with slower cases at 90 and 270 degrees.
The climber initially worked, later stalled and then drew roughly 180 A in the team's account after a firmware rollback. A motor burned out at district championship.
source_reviews.limitations: Firmware explanation was a hypothesis. The team did not establish root cause. Quoted current lacks measurement and operating context.

source_reviews.title: Typhoon Behind the Bumpers
facts: The dossier describes under-bumper acquisition, narrow swerve, a compact turret, an amp bar and a moving-camera coordinate transform.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Typhoon's core accomplishment was preserving a path from a chassis-fixed intake into a moving shooter across its yaw range. The team describes two routes around the feed, with the chosen route changing as the shooter turns. The timing penalty around the side-facing positions makes this an example of a mechanism that has full geometric coverage but uneven cycle time. The separate climber experience provides a documented failure case where holding load and getting to a hanging state were different problems.
piece_flow: A protected under-bumper pickup supplies the indexing zone in the inherited account.
The note enters one of two openings in the intake-facing arc. The feeder delivers it to the launcher with the turret at its current angle.
The team identifies two side angles where the note contacts feed rollers early and takes longer. The inherited amp bar guides a separate upward shot.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A circular feed competes with the swerve modules and support standoffs at the bottom. The rotating feed throat and wire routing define a second moving envelope above it. A moving camera, if mounted as the dossier describes, needs its image-time pose calculated from both chassis and turret motion. The inboard route must remain recoverable without dismantling the launcher.

subsystems.name: Any-angle feeder
subsystems.construction: Team confirms two entry points and rollers serving a moving receiver. Older dossier describes the inboard cage and narrow swerve packaging.
subsystems.operation: Choose the route around the turret based on receiver orientation and move the note into its feed throat.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team describes feed at any angle and a route switch during turns.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Measure acquisition-to-release time across angle and angular velocity. Static checks can miss a path switch during the handoff or a shallow angle that repeatedly slows entry.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake exit, guide/cage clearances, moving throat and roller speed coordination.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test a half-fed note as the turret crosses a route boundary and after one feed roller stalls.
subsystems.unknowns: Angle-dependent time distribution, sensing and recovery policy.

subsystems.name: Moving launcher and vision
subsystems.construction: Inherited compact continuously aiming turret, adjustable launch system and turret-mounted camera.
subsystems.operation: Track the target while driving and while receiving a note.
subsystems.team_rationale: Aim and feed can proceed together when the route stays available.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: That concurrency saves time only when the measured handoff and aim converge before the shot opportunity expires. A time offset in turret angle also becomes a pose error.
subsystems.interfaces: Turret state, cable sweep and any-angle feed should use consistent datums.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed check: inspect cable extremes and compare stationary versus moving camera pose error.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact yaw limits, camera calibration and measured shot envelope.

subsystems.name: Climber drive
subsystems.construction: Release confirms a high-load motor and reported stalls. Older dossier describes a compact worm-drive layout.
subsystems.operation: Extend and pull to lift. Holding behavior is distinct from motor capability during lift.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team cautions against reusing the design without resolving the load issue.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A self-holding or heavily reduced drive can still be inefficient and require excessive current while lifting. Diagnose load, binding, protection and supply voltage independently.
subsystems.interfaces: Hook loads, gearbox efficiency, motor settings and robot power distribution.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Motor burnout was reported. Any repeat experiment needs bounded load and temperature monitoring plus a means to unload mechanically.
subsystems.unknowns: Root cause, firmware versions, winding temperature and repeatable current traces.

revisions: Team reported a firmware rollback while troubleshooting the climber. It did not establish a successful corrective revision.
transferable_principles: Check cycle-time coverage across moving receiver positions. For a chassis-aimed design, borrow the validated staging logic and study whether two branches buy similar cycle benefit.
disconfirming_conditions: The feed benefit shrinks when the receiver is fixed or chassis turns are cheap. The climb approach fails transfer if sustained loaded current or heat exceeds the mechanism's usable window.
remaining_gaps: Readable binder body, full captions, public control paths and reliable climb load measurements.
